newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINE PLAYERS STRIKE, LEAVING FANS WITHOUT GAMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINE PLAYERS STRIKE, LEAVING FANS WITHOUT GAMES.

text.p: Despite the last-minute intervention of soccer enthusiast President Carlos Menem and pressure from superstar Diego Maradona, Argentine professional soccer players were on strike Sunday, leaving fans stranded.
Talks between the players and the Argentine Football Association (AFA) at the Labour Ministry Friday failed to reach an agreement, leading to the suspension of weekend league matches.
Even a meeting between players and Menem late Saturday was futile. The president granted the meeting "as a man of football," he said on local radio Sunday.
Menem said he had talked to his friend Maradona and was sure a quick solution will be found when talks between players and AFA resume Monday.
"I intervened because I was asked by them, but I know (AFA head) Grondona supports an end to this conflict and the whole country wants to see soccer," Menem said.
Maradona, who threw his weight behind Friday's talks, said: "This is a stupid strike, like bashing against a wall."
"I feel sorry for the people and for the players," said the star, who made a return to soccer just a month ago.
Players last Tuesday voted to strike until troubled first division side Deportivo Espanol agreed to allow six players whose contracts expired on June 30 to move to other sides.
The dispute was complicated when a judge ruled that the players counted as assets of the heavily indebted club, and so cannot leave until all creditors have been paid.
